Maps

Source: vignettes/maps.Rmd
maps.Rmd

Draw a map and join selected regions

Pass a two-letter country code to hcmap() to draw its installed boundaries. Use hc_maps() to list the available countries and regional maps.

hcmap("jp", nullColor = "rgba(106,120,124,0.16)", showInLegend = FALSE) |>
  hc_title(text = "Prefectures of Japan")

Keep the full map and supply a table for just the prefectures you want to highlight. Here joinBy matches the map’s name property to the table’s prefecture column. Hover over a highlighted prefecture to see its mountain road.

# fmt: skip
roads <- tibble::tribble(
  ~prefecture, ~road,
  "Gunma",     "Mount Haruna",
  "Tochigi",   "Irohazaka",
  "Saitama",   "Shomaru Pass",
  "Ibaraki",   "Tsukuba Fruits Line",
  "Kanagawa",  "Hakone Turnpike"
) |> mutate(selected = 1)

hcmap(
  "jp",
  data = roads,
  value = "selected",
  joinBy = c("name", "prefecture"),
  nullColor = "rgba(106,120,124,0.16)",
  borderColor = "#879392",
  borderWidth = 0.5
) |>
  hc_colorAxis(
    visible = FALSE,
    dataClasses = list(list(from = 1, to = 1, color = "rgba(177,85,45,0.65)"))
  ) |>
  hc_title(text = "Mountain roads in Japan") |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE, enableMouseWheelZoom = FALSE) |>
  hc_tooltip(
    headerFormat = "",
    pointFormat = "<b>{point.name}</b><br>{point.road}"
  )

To discover the join keys on another map, inspect its properties with get_data_from_map(). Collection paths such as "countries/jp/jp-all" also work. Use download_map_data() to save other collection boundaries for offline use.

Drill through geographic levels

Click South America, then any of its 12 countries to explore its administrative divisions. For example, Chile opens its 16 regions. Use the breadcrumbs to return one level or jump back to the continents.

Each clickable point has a drilldown ID matching a child series. All three levels use geographic coordinates and the same projection. With mapZooming = TRUE, the view zooms toward the selection as the series changes. The geometry is bundled with this article, so a click works offline.

atlas <- jsonlite::read_json("data/drilldown-south-america.json.gz")
atlas$cl <- readRDS(system.file("maps/cl.rds", package = "highcharter"))
codes <- setdiff(names(atlas), c("continents", "south_america"))
countries <- data.frame(code = codes, value = 1, drilldown = codes)

divisions <- lapply(codes, function(code) {
  list(
    id = code,
    name = atlas[[code]]$title,
    type = "map",
    mapData = atlas[[code]],
    colorAxis = FALSE,
    nullColor = "rgba(57,131,113,0.35)",
    nullInteraction = TRUE
  )
})
continents <- data.frame(code = "sa", value = 1, drilldown = "countries")
south_america <- list(
  id = "countries",
  name = "South America",
  type = "map",
  mapData = atlas$south_america,
  data = list_parse(countries),
  joinBy = c("hc-key", "code")
)

hcmap(
  atlas$continents,
  data = continents,
  value = "value",
  joinBy = c("hc-key", "code"),
  name = "Continents"
) |>
  hc_mapView(projection = list(name = "EqualEarth")) |>
  hc_plotOptions(map = list(nullColor = "rgba(106,120,124,0.16)")) |>
  hc_colorAxis(
    visible = FALSE,
    dataClasses = list(list(from = 1, to = 1, color = "rgba(24,124,101,0.62)"))
  ) |>
  hc_drilldown(
    mapZooming = TRUE,
    animation = list(duration = 650),
    series = c(list(south_america), divisions)
  ) |>
  hc_title(text = "Explore administrative divisions") |>
  hc_tooltip(
    headerFormat = "",
    pointFormat = "{point.name}",
    nullFormat = "{point.name}"
  )

Map a continuous value on a globe

An orthographic projection shows one hemisphere at a time. Drag the globe to rotate it. Join the 2024 World Bank income data to the country codes in the geographic world map. The fill uses a logarithmic scale in current US dollars per person. Gray indicates missing data. The graticule marks parallels and meridians across the oceans.

hcmap(
  "custom/world.topo.json",
  data = subset(world_income, year == 2024),
  value = "gni_per_capita",
  joinBy = c("iso-a3", "iso3"),
  name = "GNI per capita",
  nullColor = "rgba(106,120,124,0.22)",
  borderWidth = 0.3,
  zIndex = 1
) |>
  hc_add_series(
    data = geojsonio::geojson_list(sf::st_graticule()),
    type = "mapline",
    color = "rgba(86,121,130,0.35)",
    colorAxis = FALSE,
    lineWidth = 0.6,
    enableMouseTracking = FALSE,
    showInLegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  hc_mapView(projection = list(name = "Orthographic", rotation = c(60, 15))) |>
  hc_colorAxis(
    type = "logarithmic",
    stops = color_stops(colors = c("#3B245F", "#AF4664", "#F29145", "#FFEA99"))
  ) |>
  hc_title(text = "Gross national income per capita, 2024") |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE, enableMouseWheelZoom = FALSE) |>
  hc_tooltip(valuePrefix = "$", valueDecimals = 0)

Color regions by category

Use dataClasses to give discrete groups their own colors and legend entries. These European countries are grouped by standard time. Summer time is excluded.

zones <- data.frame(
  # fmt: skip
  country = c("PT", "IE", "GB", "IS", "FR", "DE", "ES", "IT", "NO", "SE",
              "PL", "AT", "CH", "FI", "EE", "LV", "LT", "GR", "RO", "BG"),
  value = c(rep(0, 4), rep(1, 9), rep(2, 7))
)
hcmap(
  "custom/europe",
  data = zones,
  value = "value",
  joinBy = c("iso-a2", "country"),
  name = "Standard time",
  nullColor = "rgba(106,120,124,0.16)"
) |>
  hc_colorAxis(
    dataClasses = list(
      list(from = 0, to = 0, name = "UTC", color = "rgba(110,79,140,0.72)"),
      list(from = 1, to = 1, name = "UTC + 1", color = "rgba(46,135,116,0.72)"),
      list(from = 2, to = 2, name = "UTC + 2", color = "rgba(192,115,43,0.72)")
    )
  ) |>
  hc_title(text = "Standard time in Europe")

Overlay point locations and a vector field

mappoint places airports by longitude and latitude. For a geographic vector field, flowmap draws an arrow between two coordinate pairs. This example places a simulated tornado over the lower Paraná, near the Río de la Plata. The footprint is enlarged so the rotation is visible at a regional scale. Arrow length shows relative speed. The airports are geographic reference points.

# fmt: skip
airports <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name,                     ~code, ~lon,   ~lat,
  "Rosario",                 "ROS", -60.79, -32.90,
  "Buenos Aires Aeroparque", "AEP", -58.42, -34.56,
  "Buenos Aires Ezeiza",     "EZE", -58.54, -34.82,
  "Montevideo Carrasco",     "MVD", -56.03, -34.84
)

wind <- data.frame(
  radius = rep(c(0.32, 0.65, 0.98), c(6, 12, 18)),
  angle = 2 * pi * c((0:5) / 6, (0:11) / 12, (0:17) / 18)
)
wind <- wind |>
  mutate(
    east = cos(angle),
    north = sin(angle),
    lon = -59.65 + radius * east / cos(-33.85 * pi / 180),
    lat = -33.85 + radius * north,
    speed = 1 - 0.6 * radius
  )

arrows <- with(
  wind,
  Map(
    function(lon, lat, east, north, speed) {
      list(
        from = c(lon, lat),
        to = c(
          lon + 0.36 * speed * (north - 0.25 * east) / cos(lat * pi / 180),
          lat - 0.36 * speed * (east + 0.25 * north)
        )
      )
    },
    lon,
    lat,
    east,
    north,
    speed
  )
)
hcmap(
  atlas$ar,
  nullColor = "rgba(106,120,124,0.12)",
  borderColor = "#ACB8B5",
  showInLegend = FALSE
) |>
  hc_add_series(
    type = "map",
    mapData = atlas$uy,
    nullColor = "rgba(106,120,124,0.12)",
    borderColor = "#ACB8B5",
    showInLegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  hc_mapView(
    projection = list(name = "WebMercator"),
    fitToGeometry = list(
      type = "MultiPoint",
      coordinates = list(c(-61.45, -35.25), c(-55.55, -32.55))
    )
  ) |>
  hc_add_series(
    data = arrows,
    type = "flowmap",
    name = "Simulated wind",
    color = "#237469",
    fillOpacity = 0.9,
    width = 1.6,
    markerEnd = list(width = 3, height = 6),
    curveFactor = 0,
    enableMouseTracking = FALSE
  ) |>
  hc_add_series(
    data = airports,
    type = "mappoint",
    name = "Airports",
    hcaes(lon = lon, lat = lat, name = name),
    color = "#934426",
    marker = list(symbol = "circle", radius = 3),
    dataLabels = list(enabled = TRUE, format = "{point.code}")
  ) |>
  hc_title(text = "A simulated wind field over the lower Paraná") |>
  hc_tooltip(headerFormat = "", pointFormat = "{point.name} ({point.code})") |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE, enableMouseWheelZoom = FALSE)

Overlay geometry on web tiles

Put a tiledwebmap series first, then add the Laguna Seca circuit. The satellite imagery loads online as you pan or zoom. The track surface, pit lane and corner apexes come from one local GeoJSON file. The translucent surface lets you see the pavement under the overlay.

path <- system.file("extdata", "laguna-seca.geojson", package = "highcharter")
circuit <- geojsonio::geojson_list(geojsonio::as.json(path))

highchart(type = "map") |>
  hc_add_series(
    type = "tiledwebmap",
    provider = list(type = "Esri", theme = "WorldImagery"),
    showInLegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  hc_add_series(
    data = circuit,
    name = c("Track surface", "Pit lane", "Apexes")
  ) |>
  hc_mapView(projection = list(name = "WebMercator"), padding = "6%") |>
  hc_plotOptions(
    map = list(color = "rgba(92,213,211,0.32)", borderColor = "#87DED7"),
    mapline = list(color = "#FFD166", lineWidth = 3),
    mappoint = list(
      color = "#FF905E",
      marker = list(symbol = "circle", radius = 4)
    ),
    series = list(dataLabels = list(enabled = FALSE))
  ) |>
  hc_title(text = "Laguna Seca") |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE, enableMouseWheelZoom = FALSE) |>
  hc_tooltip(headerFormat = "", pointFormat = "<b>{point.name}</b>") |>
  hc_legend(enabled = TRUE) |>
  hc_credits(enabled = TRUE) |>
  hc_caption(
    text = "Circuit: Track Atlas · <a href='https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright'>© OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)</a>"
  )

Toggle Track surface to compare the outline with the imagery. Track Atlas circuit data.

Bring your own GeoJSON or TopoJSON

Join a table to a TopoJSON file

Read your boundary file with jsonlite::read_json() to preserve nested coordinates. Inspect its properties to choose a join key. Here the boundary file stores district codes as text, including the leading zeros.

path <- system.file("extdata", "districts.topo.json", package = "highcharter")
districts <- jsonlite::read_json(path)
get_data_from_map(districts) |> select(name, code)
## # A tibble: 2 × 2
##   name  code 
##   <chr> <chr>
## 1 West  01   
## 2 East  02
visits <- data.frame(district_id = c("01", "02"), visits = c(18, 42))
hcmap(
  districts,
  data = visits,
  value = "visits",
  joinBy = c("code", "district_id")
) |>
  hc_colorAxis(
    minColor = "rgba(44,130,113,0.20)",
    maxColor = "rgba(44,130,113,0.85)"
  ) |>
  hc_title(text = "Visits by district") |>
  hc_tooltip(pointFormat = "{point.name}: {point.value} visits")

Layer mixed GeoJSON over a basemap

Manchester Airport is a single GeoJSON FeatureCollection. Its 26 polygons outline terminals and aprons, 254 lines trace runways and taxiways, and 136 points mark gates and other airfield features. Pass the collection to hchart() to draw the three layers. Hover over a gate to see its reference, such as Gate 21.

library(geojsonio)

path <- system.file(
  "extdata",
  "manchester-airport.geojson",
  package = "highcharter"
)
airport <- geojson_list(as.json(path))
hchart(airport, name = c("Areas", "Lines", "Points")) |>
  hc_tooltip(headerFormat = "", pointFormat = "<b>{point.name}</b>") |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE, enableMouseWheelZoom = FALSE)

The map shows the three geometry layers over a local MapLibre basemap. Toggle a layer in the legend or use the zoom buttons to explore. The GeoJSON preserves named features and labels the others with their airfield category and reference where available. Airport data from POSCON UK · Basemap example code.
